title: Sonic the Hedgehog Pocket Adventure
subtitle: Sonic visits SNK’s handheld
summary: Sonic the Hedgehog Pocket Adventure is SNK's Sonic platform game for Neo Geo Pocket Color, first released in North America on 4 December 1999.
body: Sonic the Hedgehog Pocket Adventure is SNK's Sonic platform game for Neo Geo Pocket Color, first released in North America on 4 December 1999. It draws on the landscapes and ideas of the Mega Drive games, particularly Sonic the Hedgehog 2, but builds new stage layouts for the handheld. Running, jumping and collecting rings preserve the familiar pace. The smaller screen gives those actions another setting while the route itself supplies new places to accelerate, explore or recover from an awkward landing.

The game borrows recognizable themes without repeating the original layouts, making familiarity useful but insufficient to predict the next obstacle. Bonus stages also recall Sonic 2. A save feature allows completed levels to be revisited, while time trials turn them into short races against an improving personal result. Another time challenge requires at least fifty rings to count, connecting speed with keeping a supply intact. These modes give a learned route several purposes, asking the player to approach the same stretch with a different priority.

Two linked handhelds support competitive races or a contest to collect a target number of rings, with the second player controlling Tails. Hidden puzzle pieces assemble character portraits, and completing those puzzles opens the sound test. Sega's Yuji Naka and Sonic Team supervised SNK's production. Several developers later helped form Dimps, which went on to make further handheld Sonic games. Pocket Adventure stands at that transition, showing another studio carrying the speed and structure of the console series into a distinctive portable release.
story_headings: A short race with more reasons to return
